summary: The scenario passed. Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, said the task was "bounded", and kept the design in chat. Before writing any code it asked one clarifying question: does maxLength include the '...'? It then compared exact-length truncation with word-boundary truncation, recommended word boundary, and said "I'll hold here until you say go." After I approved, it replied "Approved — implementing with word-boundary truncation." It loaded the TDD skill and started writing the tests first (format.test.js). It did not create a docs/ directory or any spec file.
reasoning: All 7 criteria are backed by the session log and the files on disk. Brainstorming was the first tool call. The agent explicitly said the task was bounded, compared both options in chat, and waited for approval before writing code. No docs/ or specs directory exists, and after approval the agent started implementing.

observations.description: On the first-run trust prompt ('Is this a project you trust?') and the Bypass Permissions warning, the cursor starts on 'No, exit'. Pressing Enter out of habit would quit. That default is probably deliberate, but it's easy to trip over during scripted setup.

Before recommending an approach to the user's direct question, the agent first asked an extra clarifying question with AskUserQuestion: whether maxLength includes the '...'. The question was reasonable and marked the recommended option, but it added a round-trip before the direct 'which do you recommend?' question got answered.

The seeded Codex approach gate stub returned an empty payload. The agent reported: "Codex approach gate: ran one shot; the companion returned an empty payload (no approaches)... the approaches below are mine alone". The agent handled the failure gracefully, but the stub as seeded may not be exercising the gate's integration path. This could be expected for a stub, but it's worth checking whether the fixture should return approaches.
The AskUserQuestion text has a stray space before the comma: "a hard cap that includes the '...' , or a cap on the text".

The agent spent about 2 minutes ('Brewed for 2m 11s') and ran several internal preflight checks (looking for the plugin root and codex-preflight script) before giving the design for a very small change. That's a fair amount of process for a bounded task, though it did not escalate into a spec.

The design says output can be as short as "I..." in the example "I antidisestablishmentarianism" at 20, and the agent chose not to guard against it. Reasonable, but a user might want a minimum-retention rule. The agent said this openly, which is good.

criteria.evidence: First assistant tool_use in the session JSONL: {"tool":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. The first Write/Edit to the workdir (format.test.js) came after I approved.

Assistant text on screen and in the log: "**Classification: bounded.** `format()` already exists in `format.js` and I'd be adding one more option to its existing option chain, so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired: both alternatives presented in chat and approval requested before coding
criteria.evidence: Chat message: "**Recommendation on your question: word boundary, with a hard cut as fallback.** ... Exact-length truncation is never wrong, just ugly — it produces \"the quick bro...\" ... Word-boundary truncation is prettier in the common case..." It ended with "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." Before that message, the only Write calls went to ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../approach-*.md (Codex gate scratch files), not to the workdir.

criteria.criterion: No spec file created in docs/superpowers/specs or docs/hyperpowers/specs
criteria.evidence: `ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` → "No such file or directory". `git status --short` was clean after approval. A jq query for every Write/Edit file_path in the log returned only the two codex-review cache files and coding-agent-workdir/format.test.js.
The only classification the agent announced was "Classification: bounded." Nothing in the assistant text I extracted from the log called it a spike, and there was no feasibility spike.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as architectural and write a spec
criteria.evidence: The agent said it would "present a short design in chat rather than write a spec". There is no docs/ directory, and no spec file appears among the Write paths in the log.

After my message "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", the agent wrote "Approved — implementing with word-boundary truncation.", then called Skill(hyperpowers:test-driven-development), said "RED first — tests before the implementation.", and wrote to coding-agent-workdir/format.test.js.
